text_en:
Safety
2.1
Intended use
The appliance controls exclusively the machine indicated on the title page.
►
Only use appliance for the intended purpose.
2.2
Technical state
If the control unit is operated when defective, safety, function and availability are
impaired.
►
Only operate the control unit when in a perfect technical condition.
►
Observe the maintenance schedule.
►
Only use genuine spare parts. See “Spare parts” chapter.
►
If the operational behaviour of the control unit changes, check the machine
for general errors.
►
Rectify general errors immediately.
►
Do not modify or alter the control unit without authorisation.
2.3
ATEX certification
The ATEX certification specifies under which conditions the control system can
be used in or attached to an Ex zone.
►
Follow the identification plate.
2.4
Staff qualification
Unqualified staff cannot recognise risks and are therefore exposed to greater
dangers.
►
Only charge qualified professional staff with tasks described in these operating instructions.
►
The operator must make sure that the staff follow the locally applicable rules
and regulations for safe and danger-conscious work.
►
The operator must define and announce the responsibility for tasks. Only
give keys and passwords to staff responsible.

Do not remove or cover up the identification plate.
4.2
Mode of operation
MEAG universal control units control, regulate and monitor processes for machines and apparatus such as scales, bagging scales, slide gates and flow balancers.
The control unit software can be configured for various applications. It is operated in the same way for all applications.
4.3
Operating modes
The following operating modes are available:
■
Bag preselection
In general, it is possible to use the device with or without preselecting the
number of bags to be filled. If a desired number of bags is entered into the
nominal bag counter, this specific number of bags are filled and the “Enable
bagging” output reverts to 0 V. Using this signal, it is possible to prevent the
device from being reactivated.
If the nominal bag counter is set to 0 (i.e. a specific number of bags has not
been preselected), the device will continue to fill bags without stopping.
■
Control cycle
The control unit fills each bag by following a fixed set of steps. If working
with control cycle “n”, once optimum actual bag weights have been reached,
only every nth bag is checked.

Filling of scales in bulk metering mode.

Filling of scales in dribble metering mode.
Upon reaching the dribble flow switch-off point,

Nominal weight

If a control cycle is undertaken, the actual bag

Top-up
If the weight is too small and the top-up function
has been enabled (TCON.TIP = ON), the remaining amount needed is added.
Enable emptying
Wait until the “Enable emptying” input is at 24 V.
Discharge
The weigh hopper is emptied.
The weigh hopper is emptied until the weight falls
below the zero tare weight (REC.EWT).
Next start
Wait for new start signal.
Calibrating
The calibration switch is in the CAL position. The
weight can only be calibrated and several parameters changed when in this position.

breadcrumb: MEAG-BAG Bagging Scale Operating Manual > 4.4 Sequence > Hal. 13
text_en:
Bagging scale weight curve (control cycle)
(1) Bulk flow switch-off point
(7) Time
(2) Bulk flow cut-off weight
(8) Step
(3) Dribble flow switch-off point
(9) Bulk flow time
(4) Dribble flow cut-off weight
(10) Dribble flow time
(5) Weight
(11) Tare weight
(6) Bag weight
Bulk metering takes place by weight or by time (according to the REC.DOSW
parameter). By default, the scale meters by weight.
The scale meters by time if the bulk flow time is < 2 seconds. This is the case
when no frequency converter is present and small weights (under 20 kg) are being metered. If a frequency converter is present, the bulk flow rate can be reduced using the REC.FFLO parameter.
Enter the bulk flow time or the weight into the REC.STRTT or REC.STRTW parameter. If these parameters are set to 0, the bag will be filled using dribble flow
instead of bulk flow.
The bulk flow cut-off weight or time are controlled automatically in such a way
that dribble metering takes place within the nominal dribble flow time REC.TDRI.
Dribble metering is always undertaken by weight using the dribble flow cut-off
weight REC.CUTW. The dribble flow cut-off weight is controlled automatically to
produce accurate bag weights.
Control cycles are used for increased performance. This means that, once the
bag weight is within the desired tolerance range, bags will only be controlled every "x" bags. For bags that are not controlled, steps 2, 5 and 6 (Zeroing, Nominal weight check, Top up) are skipped. Standard setting REC.CCYC = 10.

7.4
Scale calibration
If there are several scales present, perform this process separately for each
scale. Select the individual scales with the ADC.CHNR parameter.
Prerequisites
■
Calibration switch is in CAL position.
■
If still present, remove transportation lock from weigh hopper or weighing
platform. Weigh hopper or weighing platform hangs freely.
■
The scale is empty.
1.

►

►

for 1 second.

►

should be 30...100 % of the load capacity.
►

►

cells in turn.
►
If the weight is not displayed correctly, eliminate the fault following the
scale's operating instructions.
8.

7.5
Managing recipes
The control unit has 51 recipes (recipe numbers 0 … 50). Recipe number 0 is
the working recipe which contains the active values.
Recipes can only be written when the REC parameter group is available in the
application. We would only recommend using recipes if working with different
products. Recipe mode is always activated for some applications, e.g. bagging
controls, and does not have to be activated in such cases.

7.6
Creating recipes
Create a separate recipe for each product and bag weight.
1.
Set the desired bag weight at the REC.SIZE parameter (recipe number 0).
2.
If small bag weights (< 20 kg) are required, ensure that the bulk flow time is
not too short. Information about bulk metering: See chapter 4 “Description”..
3.
Set control cycle to 1 at REC.CCYC parameter (recipe number 0).
4.
Start the bagging process. Fill bags until the actual bag weight is correct
(MAIN.BWT) and until the actual dribble flow time (MAIN.DRIB) corresponds
to the nominal dribble flow time (REC.TDRI). Acknowledge tolerance alarms
with
.

following procedure.

for 8 seconds.

Notes for the parameter input
The letter after “Level” indicates to what extent the corresponding parameter is
locked for the change when the input lock is activated. The following values apply:
Level
Description
No information. Parameters always adjustable.
C
Parameters may be adjusted when the calibration switch is set to CAL.
L
Parameter adjustable if LOCK parameter = OFF.
Locked if LOCK parameter = LOW/MED/HIGH.
M
Parameter can be adjusted if OFF parameter = OFF/LOW.
Locked if LOCK parameter = MED/HIGH.
H
Parameter can be adjusted if LOCK parameter = OFF/LOW/MED.
Locked if LOCK parameter = HIGH.
A
Hide parameter if SYS.HIDE = ON.
The input lock is set with the SYS.LOCK parameter. It is deactivated by default.
See chapter  “Input lock”.

breadcrumb: MEAG-BAG Bagging Scale Operating Manual > 8.3.4 Parameter group PBDP (Profibus DP) > Hal. 65
text_en: Alarms and messages Alarms and messages have the following syntax: the letter A for alarm or W for warning followed by a three digit number. Example: A073. If a number follows the alarm or warning, it is a device-specific warning. The number then indicates the device number. Example: A073.2 If no further details are made about the acknowledgement, acknowledgement of the alarm depends on the SYS.ACLR parameter. See chapter  “Clear alarm”. ■ SYS.ACLR = OFF: Acknowledged automatically if the cause of the alarm has been remedied or if it changes to step 1. ■ SYS.ACLR = ON: No automatic acknowledgement. Acknowledgement only with or 24 V input “Clear alarm” possible. 9.1 BAG application alarms No. Fault Cause Remedy

product.

± 4 % of TCON.MAXB.

Check whether the inlet-metering element is leaky.

Check whether the discharge gate

Acknowledge.

is not reached within
15 seconds. When opening or closing. Only in
HCMD = AUT operating
mode.
►
Check the height adjustment.

If a component is defective, device

TOL–).

9.5
Status messages
Status messages provide information about the device status. The messages
appear alternately to the normal display and only while the status persists.
Alarms have higher priority and overwrite status messages.
Display
Status
LOCAL STOP
Device was stopped manually.
STOP
Device was stopped because 0 V is present at the 24 V input
“Enable/Start”.
c STOP
Device was stopped because no release is connected via Profibus or RS-485 (HOST).
v STOP
Device was stopped because the setpoint is too low.
m STOP
Unit was stopped because no motor current is being measured
for the grinding motors. The motors were not started or the
current measurement is not working.
Σ STOP
Device was stopped because the required total or a required
number was reached.
WAIT PROD-
UCT
Device is started but no product is present (e.g. probe is uncovered).
REFILL
Fill function is active (abnormal filling).
DISCHARGE
Emptying function (or residual discharging) is active (not normal emptying).
CAL MODE
CAL mode is active. Set calibration switch to position CAL.
SERVICE
Service mode is active, i.e. SERV.SERM = ON (outputs can
be set).
LOCAL
The device is operated locally. Only if REMOTE input is active
and 0 V is on.
MANUAL
The device is operated manually. No automatic control sequence.
EMERGENCY
Device is in emergency operation.
TEACHING
Device is in learning mode.
HIGH SETP
Setpoint is too high. The nominal value is limited to the maximum value.
SIM ON
Simulator mode is activated, i.e. SERV.SIMM = ON.

breadcrumb: MEAG-BAG Bagging Scale Operating Manual > 9.2 Basic alarms > Hal. 72
text_en:
Display
Status
SIM FREEZE
Simulator mode is on but passive.
TEST
Device is in test mode.
LOW SETP
Setpoint is too low. The nominal value is limited to the minimum or 0.
WARM UP
Wait until the AD converter is stable.
STOP OPEN
OK
Device is stopped. All elements are in home position. The machine must not be switched off or opened.
OVERLOAD
The grinding motor utilisation has exceeded 130 %. The grinding rollers were disengaged.
SAVE BUSY
Automatic grinding gap adjustment has sent a save request.
But the message was not acknowledged by the host system.
HL INLET
The inlet probe is reporting covered (0V). This message is only output if TCON.HL IN = DIG_IN.
9.6
Short messages
Short messages are operating aids. They appear once at the touch of a button.
Some of the following messages are application-specific, i.e. they do not occur
with every control unit.
Display
Status
OK
Input detected and applied.
Example: If a recipe was loaded.
LOCK
Changing of the parameter is locked.
See chapter  “Input lock”.
PROTECT
Recipes are protected against overwriting. Saving the recipes
is not possible.
See chapter  “Write protection for recipe during SAVE”.
DATA INIT
Initialisation is executed. Control unit is reset to default values.
See chapter  “Basic initialisation of all parameters”.
SET ZERO
Zero adjustment is executed.
See chapter  “Zero scale”.
SET CAL
Calibration is executed.
See chapter  “Calibration weight”.
SET TARE
Taring is executed.
WT INIT
Weight values are re-initialised.
Example: If ADC.DIV is adjusted.
WAIT
The device processes an order and prompts the operator to
wait.
Do not operate the control unit while WAIT is displayed.
CLEAR
Data is deleted.
ESC
Change was aborted.
Example: If
is pressed during a change.

text_en:
Foreword
The operating instructions are to be distributed to those persons responsible for
operating and monitoring the device.
The operating instructions contain the information necessary for installation, operation and maintenance.
Those tasks not requiring special knowledge or skills were not included in the instructions.
Repair instructions above and beyond the regular maintenance tasks to be performed are not provided in the instructions.
Important notes
•
Receiving Inspection
Immediately upon receipt, perform a visual inspection of the control unit as defined by the delivery contract.
•
Storage
If the control unit will not immediately be installed in its final destination, store
the unit in a protected location to prevent damage due to weather and foreign
material.
•
Installation
All installation specifications delivered along with the control unit must be followed during installation.
•
Model types
Should the documentation provided with the control unit describe other versions of the unit, only that information which pertains to the version of the control unit that was delivered to the recipient shall apply. All features and specifications are subject to technical modification without notice prior to shipment.
•
Duty of instruction
The unit may only be operated and maintained by trained and qualified personnel. Prior to initial operation, all personnel that will be operating the unit
must familiarize themselves with the documentation provided.
Further documentation
Other documents are available for reference:

text_en:
Safety
Note:
The operating instructions must be kept near the control unit.
1.1
Intended use
The control unit is intended to control only the device shown on the title page of
this document.
It is not intended for any other use.
1.2
Duty of instruction
The operator is responsible for the training and safety of the operating personnel.
For this reason, it is very important that these operating instructions actually be distributed to these persons.
Operating personnel responsible for the installation, operation or maintenance of
the control unit must have read and understood these operating instructions.
1.3
Accident prevention
The control unit complies with the international safety standard.
For your own safety, please observe all accident prevention and safety regulations
that are contained in these operating instructions and that apply locally.
Note:
Warning and instruction plates must be kept clean and must not be removed or
covered.
Immediately replace any illegible warning and instruction plates.
1.4
Operation
The control unit may only be operated by instructed and trained personnel. Personnel must be familiar with all display and operational elements.
1.5
Electrical installation
Have authorized personnel perform the installation procedures.
•
Observe regulations issued by local safety authorities.
•
Secure the supply lines according to local regulations.
•
Check the operating voltage and frequency with respect to the information provided on the identification plate and in the control cabinet.
•
Connect the control unit power supply according to the connection diagram.
•
When setting up or repairing the control unit, make sure that the power supply
is interrupted by disconnecting all poles and that it cannot be restarted.
Check the electrical installation on a regular basis.
•
Repair or replace defective installations or devices immediately.

text_en: Commissioning Basic parameters are configured ex works. Note: To change the parameters, the control unit must be in step 0 (Calibrating) or step 1 (Standby). (For current step, see WT.) Stop the scale for this purpose. This happens when the device is stopped. The control process can also be forced into step 0. Set the calibration switch to CAL and turn the input voltage on and off. 4.1 Basic settings 1. Set the parameter SYS.TYP to CHECK (may only be adjustable when calibration switch = CAL). If this is not the case, set the most important parameters with the input assistant. Calibration switch = CAL. Using the parameter SYS.TYP, press the "F" key. The assistant is activated. Using the arrow button, select each parameter directly. The assistant is automatically exited after the last parameter. SYS.TYP displays CHECK. 2. If the scale's setpoints are being configured remotely, set the SYS.REM parameter (analog, serial, or Profibus). 4.2 Calibrating the scale 3. Remove the transportation locks from the weigh hopper. 4. Make sure that the weighing platform is clear and can be moved horizontally in all directions. 5. Turn on the control unit. Wait at least 10 minutes before beginning the calibration process. 6. Set the calibration switch S2 on the main circuit board to CAL. 7. Perform zeroing with the ADC.ZERO parameter by pressing the "F" key. A rotating clock symbol is displayed. Do not interfere with the scale while it is being zeroed. 8. Using the ADC.CALW parameter, enter the total weight of the applied calibration weights. (The calibration weight should be roughly 30...100% of the load capacity.) 9. Put the calibrations weights in the centre. 10. Perform calibration with the ADC.CALW parameter by pressing the "F" key. A rotating clock symbol is displayed. Do not interfere with the scale while

breadcrumb: MEAG Checkweigher (CHECK) Operating Instructions > 4.3 Preparation of recipes > Hal. 19
text_en:
4.3
Preparation of recipes
Create a separate recipe for each bag weight.
1. Set the recipe number of the desired recipe to REC.NR.
2. Set the nominal bag weight (net weight) using parameter REC.SIZE.
3. Set the empty bag weight (tare weight) using parameter REC.EBAG.
4. Set the tolerance limits to parameters REC.T1+ / REC.T1–
(tolerance limits for bag ejection)
5. Possibly set the tolerance limits to parameters REC.T2+ / REC.T2–
(tolerance limits for alarm and line stop)
To activate the recipe, load it into the working recipe: Using the parameter LOAD,
enter the desired recipe number.

breadcrumb: MEAG Checkweigher (CHECK) Operating Instructions > 5.1 Brief description > Hal. 20
text_en:
Functional description
5.1
Brief description
The function CHECK allows bags (and other packages) to be checked on the conveyor belt. The conveyor belt acts as a scale and for this reason stands on DMS
load cells. If a bag is on the scale (24 V input signal from a light barrier), the weight
is checked. If the weight falls below or exceeds the weight of the tolerance, a 24 V
output signal is sent. This signal allows the bag to be ejected for example.
The device can be remote-controlled via Profibus DP.
The nominal bag weight (net weight), the empty weight of the bag and the tolerances are stored in recipes.
5.2
Steps
Once the scale has been turned on, steps 1 through 4 are executed in cycles.
Step
Meaning
Description
Standby
The control unit remains in standby mode after a process has been
aborted or in the event of an alarm.
Bag in the light
barrier
The bag end is detected.
Delay time until
weight acceptance
Wait until the weight is accepted from the bag end. The basic time is
set to parameter TCON.TSTD. The recipe-dependant time REC.TSD+
is added.
Data transmission
Data transmission with the time TCON.TDO
(transmission of weight information to the digital outputs)
Switches back to step 1 after the time TDO.
Stays in this step if the alarm output has been affected.
Calibrating
The calibration switch S2 is on CAL. Only during this step is it possible
to adjust the weight or make changes to the parameters.

Older alarms can be displayed by pressing the "F" and "-" keys. The second-to-last alarm will be displayed as ERR.-1, etc. Go back to the previous alarm by pressing the "F" and "+" keys. By pressing only the "F" key, it is possible to switch between the entire alarm message, date and time. EVT List of events The last event will be displayed as EVT.0 E001 . For operation, see parameter ERR. ALLEVT List of alarms and events Alarms and events are both shown. For operation, see parameter ERR. CPU Computer load Displayed on the left: Current computer load in %. Displayed on the right: Max. time in ms for a programme cycle. If necessary, max. value can be reset by pressing the "F" key. Software runtime error
Programme runtime error occurred (problem with the software or hardware).
−
Turn the device off and back on again.

A005
NO24V
24V power supply
Voltage is too low (<18 V)
−
Measure the voltage on X1.
−
If the voltage measures <18 V, look for

−

breadcrumb: MEAG Checkweigher (CHECK) Operating Instructions > 7.2 Basic alarms > Hal. 40 [A006]
text_en:
A006
DATALOST
Loss of data
Loss of data in the battery-buffered RAM.
The parameters and diverse data are initialised to their default values.
May occur once after a software download.
−
Check the fit of the battery base.
−
Acknowledge the alarm if new software
was loaded.
−
To acknowledge the alarm:
Disconnect the control unit from the
mains.
Wait 15 min.
Turn on the control unit.
If the alarm is repeated, replace the
battery.

breadcrumb: MEAG Checkweigher (CHECK) Operating Instructions > 7.5 Operational status messages > Hal. 45
text_en:
7.5
Operational status messages
Operational status messages give an overview of the operational status of the device.
The messages are displayed alternately with the normal display and only as long
as the status lasts.
Alarms are of higher priority and overwrite operational status messages.
Message
Meaning
LOCAL STOP
Device has been stopped manually.
STOP
Device has been stopped because 0V is displayed on the 24V input "Enable/Start".
c STOP
Device has been stopped because no release is connected via Profibus or
RS-485 (HOST).
v STOP
Device has been stopped because the setpoint is too low.
∑ STOP
Device has been stopped because the required total or a required number
has been reached.
WAIT PRODUCT
Device has been started but no product is present (e.g., probe is uncovered).
REFILL
Fill function is active (abnormal filling).
DISCHARGE
Empty function (or residual discharge function) is active (abnormal discharge).
CAL MODE
CAL mode is active (switch is in the CAL position).
SERVICE
Service mode is active (outputs may be set).
LOCAL
Device is being operated locally (only if REMOTE input is active and 0 V is
on).
MANUAL
Device is being operated manually (control operations not occurring automatically).
EMERGENCY
Device is running in emergency mode.
TEACHING
Device is running in teaching mode.
HIGH SETP
Setpoint is too high. The setpoint is set at the maximum value.
SIM ON
Simulator mode is on and active.
SIM FREEZE
Simulator mode is on but passive.
TEST
Device is running in test mode.
LOW SETP
Setpoint is too low. Setpoint is set at the minimum or at 0.
WARM UP
Wait until the AD converter is stable.

breadcrumb: MEAG Checkweigher (CHECK) Operating Instructions > 7.6 Updates > Hal. 46
text_en:
7.6
Updates
Updates serve to help during operation of the device. They appear only once when
a key is pressed.
Message
Meaning
Applications
OK
Input has been recognized and accepted.
E.g., when a recipe is loaded.
LOCK
The edit parameter function is locked.
E.g., the edit parameter function is
locked with SYS.LOCK.
PROTECT
Recipes are protected from being
overwritten. The save recipe function
is locked.
E.g., recipe overwrite protection
REC.PROT = ON
DATA INIT
Perform the initialization process.
Caution: Parameters are being set to
default values.
With SYS.INIT
SET ZERO
Perform zeroing.
E.g., during the zeroing process
(ADC.ZERO)
SET CAL
Perform calibration.
E.g., during calibration (ADC.CALW)
SET TARE
Perform tare procedure.
E.g., when taring DMS-T
WT INIT
Reinitialize weight values.
Caution: Data may be lost.
E.g., when ADC.DIV is adjusted.
WAIT
Please wait until the WAIT message
has disappeared.
CLEAR
Data are being erased.
E.g., event reports.
ESC
Editing cancelled.
"LT" key was pressed during the editing
process.
OCCUPIED
Interface is busy.
E.g., when SIO is connected to the host
interface and must be reconnected to
an external device.
NO EDIT
Edit function is not possible.
E.g., display parameters (may never be
edited).
NO CAL
Editing may only take place in CAL
mode.
E.g., display parameters (may not be
edited).
NO LOCAL
Editing may only take place in LOCAL
mode.
E.g., display parameters (may not be
edited).
NO STOP
Editing may only take place when the
device has been stopped.
E.g., display parameters (may not be
edited).
NO SETVAL
No setpoint is present.
E.g., it is possible to start the device
without a setpoint.
ASSIST ON
The input assistant has been turned
on.
ASSIST OFF
The input assistant has been turned
off.
OUT OF
RANGE
The value that was entered lies outside of the possible setting range.

text_en:
2.1
Intended use
The device controls exclusively the machine indicated on the title page.
-
Use the device only for its intended purpose.
2.2
Technical condition
If the control unit is operated when defective, then safety, function and availability will be compromised.
-
Only operate the control unit when in perfect technical condition.
-
Comply with the maintenance schedule.
-
Only use original spare parts.
-
If the operational behavior of the control unit changes, check the machine for
general errors.
-
Rectify faults immediately.
-
Do not convert or modify the control unit without authorization.
2.3
ATEX designation
The ATEX designation specifies under which conditions the control system can
be used in or attached to an Ex zone.
-
Note the nameplate.
2.4
Personnel qualifications
Unqualified personnel cannot recognize risks and are thus exposed to greater
danger.
-
Only charge qualified personnel with tasks described in these operating instructions.
-
The plant operator must ensure that personnel comply with local laws and
regulations for safe and hazard-conscious work.
-
The plant operator must assign responsibilities and make these known. Provide keys and passwords only to assigned personnel.

Nameplate (example)
Do not remove or cover up the nameplate.
4.2
Operating principle
MEAG universal control units control, regulate and monitor processes for machines and apparatus such as scales, bagging scales, slide gates and flow balancers.
The control unit software can be configured for various applications. It is operated in the same way for all applications.
4.3
Operating modes
The following operating modes are available:
Ŷ
Continuous scale (intake weigher, check weigher)
The scale registers the weighed product. "Residual discharge" adds a surplus dump to the total. Nominal rate   0 / nominal total weight   0.
Ŷ
Preselected rate (mill feed B1 scale)
The scale determines the throughput. The system functions on the basis of
the preselected rate. Nominal rate > 0. See TCON.FMAX and USER.FLO/
FLOS parameters.
Ŷ
Loading scale
The scale doses a preselected nominal total weight of product (ː1 S). It is
also possible to work with a nominal rate.

breadcrumb: MEAG-DUMP Dump Scale Operating Manual > 4.4 Sequence > Hal. 11
text_en:
4.4
Sequence
Steps 2 to 8 are processed cyclically.
Step
no.
Name
Description
Initial situation
The control is waiting. The scale is not on. Nothing is released or the total weight has been reached.
Dosing
Fill the weighing container. The control unit waits until the
nominal dump weight (MAIN.DWTS) has been reached or
the process is aborted by "Residual discharge".
Gross
weight
Saves the gross weight during standstill. Pressure compensation valve is open.
Emptying
release
Waits until there is 24 V at the "Emptying release" input (only if TCON.DIPB   ON or ON_P).
Emptying
Empties the weighing container until the weight is below the
zero tare (TCON.MEWT).
Close
scale
Closes the discharge gate. With monitoring if the "Scale
closed" probe is present.
Tare
Saves the tare during standstill. Calculates the actual dump
and the total weight. Pressure compensation valve is open.
Batch
end
When in "Preselected rate" mode. Waits until a new cycle
begins. When TCON.IMOD   FULL or FULLR, the control
waits until the probe in the scale upper surge hopper is covered.
Calibrating
The calibration switch is in the CAL position. Calibrating the
weight and modifying certain parameters is only possible in
this position.

text_en: 3. Calibrate scale: - Select ADC.CALW parameter. - Enter the total weight of the calibration weights. The calibration weight should be 30...100 % of the load capacity. - Fasten the calibrations weights symmetrically in the intended places. - Press for 1 second. ൺ A rotating clock symbol is displayed. Do not touch the scale during this process. 4. Select ADC.WT parameter. 5. Check whether the value displayed matches the calibration weight value. 6. Remove the calibration weights. ൺ 0 is displayed for ADC.WT parameter. 7. For scales with several load cells: - Place a weight of 0.1 ... 20 kg (depending on scale size) on each of the load cells in turn. - If the weight is not displayed correctly, eliminate the fault following the scale s operating instructions. 8. Set calibration switch on main circuit board to RUN. 7.5 Starting/stopping the scale When starting, the scale goes from step 1 to step 2. The inlet slide gate opens. The scale waits for the product. Stopping exits the started cycle. The scale goes to step 1 after the emptying process. If TCON.DSTO ON, the cycle also stops during "Residual discharge". The following applies depending on the value of the SYS.REM parameter (local or remote control): Ŷ Local operation (SYS.REM LOC) Ƒ Press <S1> key to start the scale even if the digital release input is being used. If TCON.KSTO ON, the scale can also be stopped again using the <S1> key. Ƒ If TCON.KSTO OFF, go to the ADC.WT parameter and press the <S4> key until the scale is in step 1. Ŷ Remote control (SYS.REM REMS or REMP) Ƒ The scale is started and stopped through remote control via the serial interface or the Profibus DP. Ƒ If the digital input is being used for enabling, this function takes precedence. 7.6 Managing recipes The control system has 51 recipes (recipe numbers 0 ... 50). Recipe number 0 is the working recipe which contains the active values. Recipes can only be written when the REC parameter group is available in the application. We would only recommend using recipes if working with different products. Recipe mode is always activated for some applications, e.g. bagging controls, and does not have to be activated in such cases.

The letter after "Step" indicates to what extent the corresponding parameter is
locked for the change when the input lock is activated. The following values apply:
Step Description

Parameter can be adjusted if LOCK parameter   OFF.
Locked if LOCK parameter   LOW/MED/HIGH.
M

Locked if LOCK parameter   MED/HIGH.

text_en: Alarms and messages have the following syntax: The letter A for alarm or W for warning followed by a three-digit number. Example: A073. If a number follows the alarm or warning, it is a device-specific warning. The number then indicates the device number. Example: A073.2 If no further details are provided about the acknowledgement, the acknowledgement of the alarm depends on the "SYS.ACLR" parameter. See page 45, parameter "SYS.ACLR". Ŷ "SYS.ACLR   OFF"   Automatic acknowledgement if the cause of the alarm has been remedied or when a change has been made to Step 1. Ŷ "SYS.ACLR"   ON: No automatic acknowledgement. Acknowledgement only possible with or 24 V input "Clear alarm". 9.1 Application alarms

breadcrumb: MEAG-DUMP Dump Scale Operating Manual > 9.1 Application alarms > Hal. 71 [A020]
text_en:
A020 MOVE
Cause
Correction
The scale weight is not at a standstill.
-
Avoid violently shaking the scale.
-
Check inlet and outlet elements for leaks.
-
Remove anything influencing aspiration.
-
Increase the maximum downtime TCON.TSTA or downtime tolerance ADC.MOT.

breadcrumb: MEAG-DUMP Dump Scale Operating Manual > 9.1 Application alarms > Hal. 71 [A021]

Cause
Correction
The scale is not emptied within the
maximum allotted emptying time.
The discharge gate does not open
or only opens part way.
-
Increase the maximum emptying time TCON.TDMA.

text_en:
Foreword
The operating instructions are to be distributed to those persons responsible for
operating and monitoring the device.
The operating instructions contain the information necessary for installation, operation and maintenance.
Those tasks not requiring special knowledge or skills were not included in the instructions.
Repair instructions above and beyond the regular maintenance tasks to be performed are not provided in the instructions.
Important notes
•
Receiving Inspection
Immediately upon receipt, perform a visual inspection of the control unit as defined by the delivery contract.
•
Storage
If the control unit will not immediately be installed in its final destination, store
the unit in a protected location to prevent damage due to weather and foreign
material.
•
Installation
All installation specifications delivered along with the control unit must be followed during installation.
•
Model types
Should the documentation provided with the control unit describe other versions of the unit, only that information which pertains to the version of the control unit that was delivered to the recipient shall apply. All features and specifications are subject to technical modification without notice prior to shipment.
•
Duty of instruction
The unit may only be operated and maintained by trained and qualified personnel. Prior to initial operation, all personnel that will be operating the unit
must familiarize themselves with the documentation provided.
Further documentation
Other documents are available for reference:
Name
ID number
Profibus DP protocol
Description of the RS-485 serial interface
MEAF-66435
Note:
These operating instructions apply as of programme version
DC_SCALE V10A.

text_en:
Safety
Note:
The operating instructions must be kept near the control unit.
1.1
Intended use
The control unit is intended to control only the device shown on the title page of
this document.
It is not intended for any other use.
1.2
Duty of instruction
The operator is responsible for the training and safety of the operating personnel.
For this reason, it is very important that these operating instructions actually be distributed to these persons.
Operating personnel responsible for the installation, operation or maintenance of
the control unit must have read and understood these operating instructions.
1.3
Accident prevention
The control unit complies with the international safety standard.
For your own safety, please observe all accident prevention and safety regulations
that are contained in these operating instructions and that apply locally.
Note:
Warning and instruction plates must be kept clean and must not be removed or
covered.
Immediately replace any illegible warning and instruction plates.
1.4
Operation
The control unit may only be operated by instructed and trained personnel. Personnel must be familiar with all display and operational elements.
1.5
Electrical installation
Have authorized personnel perform the installation procedures.
•
Observe regulations issued by local safety authorities.
•
Secure the supply lines according to local regulations.
•
Check the operating voltage and frequency with respect to the information provided on the identification plate and in the control cabinet.
•
Connect the control unit power supply according to the connection diagram.
•
When setting up or repairing the control unit, make sure that the power supply
is interrupted by disconnecting all poles and that it cannot be restarted.
Check the electrical installation on a regular basis.
•
Repair or replace defective installations or devices immediately.

doc_title: MEAG Differential Dosing Scale (DIFF) Operating Instructions
breadcrumb: MEAG Differential Dosing Scale (DIFF) Operating Instructions > 4.1 Basic settings > Hal. 20
text_en:
Commissioning
Basic parameters are configured ex works.
Note:
To change the parameters, the control unit must be in step 0 (Calibrating) or
step 1 (Standby). (For current step, see WT.) Stop the scale for this purpose.
The control process can also be forced into step 0. Set the calibration switch to
CAL and turn the input voltage on and off.
4.1
Basic settings
1. Are the parameters configured to SYS.TYP = DIFF and TCON.DTYP = type of
scale?
If not: adjust parameter SYS.TY to DIFF (parameters may only be adjusted
when the calibration switch is on CAL; control restarts). Use the input assistant
to configure the most important parameters. Using the parameter SYS.TYP,
press the "F" key. The assistant is activated. Using the arrow button, select
each parameter directly. The assistant is automatically exited after the last parameter. SYS.TYP displays DIFF.
2. If the scale's setpoints are being configured remotely, set the SYS.REM parameter (analog, serial, or Profibus).
3. Using the TCON.MODE parameter, configure the scale to the corresponding
operating mode (flow rate controller, flowmeter, small charge metering). See
also Operating Modes.
4. If the scale is an admixing scale, set the parameter TCON.ADDM to ON and
configure the rate of the control scale on parameter TCON.MAST.
5. If you are working with only one product or with very similar products, enter the
specific weight using parameter REC.DENS (REC.NR = 0).
(For very different products, see "Preparation of recipes".)

doc_title: MEAG Differential Dosing Scale (DIFF) Operating Instructions
breadcrumb: MEAG Differential Dosing Scale (DIFF) Operating Instructions > 4.2 Scale calibration > Hal. 21
text_en: 4.2 Scale calibration 1. Remove the transportation locks from the weigh hopper. 2. Make sure that the weigh hopper hangs freely. 3. Turn on the control unit. Wait at least 10 minutes before beginning the calibration process. 4. Clear off the scale: press the "Empty" key. 5. Set the calibration switch S2 on the main circuit board to CAL. 6. Perform zeroing with the ADC.ZERO parameter by pressing the "F" key. A rotating clock symbol is displayed. Do not interfere with the scale while it is being zeroed. 7. Using the ADC.CALW parameter, enter the total weight of the applied calibration weights. (The calibration weight should be roughly 30...100% of the load capacity.) 8. Calibration weights should be mounted symmetrically onto the places provided on the weigh hopper. 9. Calibrate using the ADC.CALW parameter by pressing the "F" key. A rotating clock symbol is displayed. Do not interfere with the scale while it is being calibrated. 10. Using the ADC.WT parameter, check the weight display for the calibration weight. 11. Remove the calibration weights. 12. The weight displayed on the ADC.WT parameter must be 0. 13. Only for scales with 3 weigh cells: Place a weight of 1kg onto each of the weigh cells, one after the other, and look at the display. If the displayed weight values are the same as that of the weight, all weigh cells are functioning properly and have been properly installed and wired. If the values are not the same, correct the error(s) by following the scale's operating instructions. 14. Set the calibration switch S2 on the main circuit board to RUN. 4.3 Preparation of recipes Create a separate recipe for each product. If you are working with recipes, configure parameter TCON.RECM = USER/MAIN. 1. If there is no recipe, see number 3 to

breadcrumb: MEAG Differential Dosing Scale (DIFF) Operating Instructions > 4.2 Scale calibration > Hal. 21
text_en: following the scale's operating instructions. 14. Set the calibration switch S2 on the main circuit board to RUN. 4.3 Preparation of recipes Create a separate recipe for each product. If you are working with recipes, configure parameter TCON.RECM = USER/MAIN. 1. If there is no recipe, see number 3 to continue. 2. To load a recipe: Using the LOAD parameter, enter the recipe number from a similar recipe (similar specific weight). Press S6 for >1 second until it flashes and select the desired recipe number by pressing the "+ / -" key. Confirm by pressing S6 (→ OK). 3. Set the desired weight on the REC.DENS parameter (recipe number 0). For MWBG or MSDG, continue with number 6. 4. Switch on learning mode using parameter MAIN.TEACHF (F key). Begin metering with the highest possible rate (30…100 % of maximum flow rate). 5. Wait until the factor has changed using parameter MAIN.TEACHF. 6. To save a recipe: Enter the desired recipe number using the SAVE parameter. The working recipe [0] is stored in the preselected memory. 7. Only for devices with screw metering: As a control, stop the device and restart. The rate setpoint should be quickly reached.

doc_title: MEAG Differential Dosing Scale (DIFF) Operating Instructions
breadcrumb: MEAG Differential Dosing Scale (DIFF) Operating Instructions > 5.1 Operating modes > Hal. 22
text_en: Functional description 5.1 Operating modes Flow rate control (TCON.MODE = FLOCON) Control of discharge rate (actual rate) to the predefined nominal rate (FLOS). The actual rate is calculated by determining the weight reduction in the weigh hopper. If the weight in the weigh hopper reaches a minimum weight (lower switch point TCON.LLEV), an output for the automatic product feed is activated. Further metering takes place during the filling process. This operating mode is possible with or without nominal weight. If the nominal weight = 0, the device will continue to meter without stopping. Flowmeter (TCON.MODE = FLOMET) Determining a given product flow (weight and rate). The discharge rate is controlled according to the feeding rate so that there is always a constant level in the weigh hopper (TCON.NLEV). Small charge metering (TCON.MODE = CHARGE) Exact weight metering to a preselected nominal weight (Σ1 S). The screw rpm remains constant according to the predefined nominal rate. If the nominal weight cannot be metered with a container fill, it will be automatically filled. Further metering does not take place during the filling process. The operating mode is very specific as the weight before and after the metering is determined when the screws are at a standstill. Small charge metering or flow rate controller (TCON.MODE = CHAFLO) According to the nominal weight, an automatic selection is made on whether the device is to work in the operating mode "small charge metering" or "flow rate control". Small nominal weights contained in a container fill are metered according to the principle of "small charge metering". Larger nominal weights according to the principle of "flow rate control". In this mode, the nominal weight is metered constantly without interruption. Admixing mode (TCON.ADDM = ON) The admixing mode is not an independent operating mode and can only be

doc_title: MEAG Differential Dosing Scale (DIFF) Operating Instructions
breadcrumb: MEAG Differential Dosing Scale (DIFF) Operating Instructions > 5.1 Operating modes > Hal. 22
text_en: are metered according to the principle of "small charge metering". Larger nominal weights according to the principle of "flow rate control". In this mode, the nominal weight is metered constantly without interruption. Admixing mode (TCON.ADDM = ON) The admixing mode is not an independent operating mode and can only be additionally selected in the operating mode "flow rate control". In the admixing mode a product is metered percentage-wise to a control scale. For this, the two setpoints control scale rate and admixing percentage are calculated to the internal nominal rate. The rate of the control scale is transmitted to the MEAG via the analog flow input AI_0.1.

doc_title: MEAG Differential Dosing Scale (DIFF) Operating Instructions
breadcrumb: MEAG Differential Dosing Scale (DIFF) Operating Instructions > 5.2 Steps > Hal. 23
text_en:
5.2
Steps
The weighing process consists of various steps. Steps 2 through 6 are executed in
cycles.
Step
Meaning
Description
Standby
The control unit is in standby mode.
The scale is not activated, no enabling takes place or the total weight
is reached.
Fill container
Output "product feed" turns on. Product is requested to fill the scale to
the upper switch point. The filling process is temporally monitored.
Further metering takes place at the output.
Deaeration follow-up time
Output "aspiration" is activated according to the set "deaeration follow-up time". This step is only carried out if the container was filled up
in step 2.
Transient response
Waiting period according to the set "transient response" until measurement begins.
Measuring time
During the measuring time, the measurement points for calculating
the rate are saved. The measuring time and number of measurement
points are automatically selected depending on the nominal rate and
the current control range.
Calculations
Calculating the actual rate and the total weights. For the operating
rate "flow rate control", the control signal for the slide gate or the
screw rpm is calculated and sent using the nominal/actual difference.
Emptying
The weigh hopper is emptied at a constant rate.
Filling up
Output "product feed" automatically fills the scale. For the types with
screw metering, the screws are also filled when a nominal rate has
been preselected.
Meter small
charge
Exact weight metering to a preselected nominal weight. The screw
rpm remains constant depending on the nominal rate.
Calibrating
The calibration switch S2 is on CAL. Only during this step is it possible to adjust the weight or make changes to the parameters.

Turn the device off and back on again.
−

SERV.SADR and contact the Bühler

text_en:
A005
NO24V
24V power supply
Voltage is too low (<18 V)
−
Measure the voltage on X1.
−
If the voltage measures <18 V, look for
the cause. Defective mains component
or overload.
−
If the voltage measures >18 V, replace
the main circuit board.

doc_title: MEAG Differential Dosing Scale (DIFF) Operating Instructions

text_en:
A006
DATALOST
Loss of data
Loss of data in the battery-buffered RAM.
The parameters and diverse data are initialised to their default values.
May occur once after a software download.
−
Check the fit of the battery base.
−
Acknowledge the alarm if new software
was loaded.
−
To acknowledge the alarm:
Disconnect the control unit from the
mains.
Wait 15 min.
Turn on the control unit.
If the alarm is repeated, replace the
battery.

fallen below the normal limits. See also
Parameter WT and ADC.MAXR.
−
Recalibrate.
−
Check X313 jumpers.
−
Clear foreign material from the weigh
hopper. (e.g., Have the transportation
locks been removed?)
−

set it to 0.
−
Check the installation position of the
load cells.

doc_title: MEAG Differential Dosing Scale (DIFF) Operating Instructions
breadcrumb: MEAG Differential Dosing Scale (DIFF) Operating Instructions > 7.5 Operational status messages > Hal. 59
text_en:
7.5
Operational status messages
Operational status messages give an overview of the operational status of the device.
The messages are displayed alternately with the normal display and only as long
as the status lasts.
Alarms are of higher priority and overwrite operational status messages.
Message
Meaning
LOCAL STOP
Device has been stopped manually.
STOP
Device has been stopped because 0V is displayed on the 24V input "Enable/Start".
c STOP
Device has been stopped because no release is connected via Profibus or
RS-485 (HOST).
v STOP
Device has been stopped because the setpoint is too low.
∑ STOP
Device has been stopped because the required total or a required number
has been reached.
WAIT PRODUCT
Device has been started but no product is present (e.g., probe is uncovered).
REFILL
Fill function is active (abnormal filling).
DISCHARGE
Empty function (or residual discharge function) is active (abnormal discharge).
CAL MODE
CAL mode is active (switch is in the CAL position).
SERVICE
Service mode is active (outputs may be set).
LOCAL
Device is being operated locally (only if REMOTE input is active and 0 V is
on).
MANUAL
Device is being operated manually (control operations not occurring automatically).
EMERGENCY
Device is running in emergency mode.
TEACHING
Device is running in teaching mode.
HIGH SETP
Setpoint is too high. The setpoint is set at the maximum value.
SIM ON
Simulator mode is on and active.
SIM FREEZE
Simulator mode is on but passive.
TEST
Device is running in test mode.
LOW SETP
Setpoint is too low. Setpoint is set at the minimum or at 0.
WARM UP
Wait until the AD converter is stable.

doc_title: MEAG Differential Dosing Scale (DIFF) Operating Instructions
breadcrumb: MEAG Differential Dosing Scale (DIFF) Operating Instructions > 7.6 Updates > Hal. 60
text_en:
7.6
Updates
Updates serve to help during operation of the device. They appear only once when
a key is pressed.
Message
Meaning
Applications
OK
Input has been recognized and accepted.
E.g., when a recipe is loaded.
LOCK
The edit parameter function is locked.
E.g., the edit parameter function is
locked with SYS.LOCK.
PROTECT
Recipes are protected from being
overwritten. The save recipe function
is locked.
E.g., recipe overwrite protection
REC.PROT = ON
DATA INIT
Perform the initialization process.
Caution: Parameters are being set to
default values.
With SYS.INIT
SET ZERO
Perform zeroing.
E.g., during the zeroing process
(ADC.ZERO)
SET CAL
Perform calibration.
E.g., during calibration (ADC.CALW)
SET TARE
Perform tare procedure.
E.g., when taring DMS-T
WT INIT
Reinitialize weight values.
Caution: Data may be lost.
E.g., when ADC.DIV is adjusted.
WAIT
Please wait until the WAIT message
has disappeared.
CLEAR
Data are being erased.
E.g., event reports.
ESC
Editing cancelled.
"LT" key was pressed during the editing
process.
OCCUPIED
Interface is busy.
E.g., when SIO is connected to the host
interface and must be reconnected to
an external device.
NO EDIT
Edit function is not possible.
E.g., display parameters (may never be
edited).
NO CAL
Editing may only take place in CAL
mode.
E.g., display parameters (may not be
edited).
NO LOCAL
Editing may only take place in LOCAL
mode.
E.g., display parameters (may not be
edited).
NO STOP
Editing may only take place when the
device has been stopped.
E.g., display parameters (may not be
edited).
NO SETVAL
No setpoint is present.
E.g., it is possible to start the device
without a setpoint.
ASSIST ON
The input assistant has been turned
on.
ASSIST OFF
The input assistant has been turned
off.
OUT OF
RANGE
The value that was entered lies outside of the possible setting range.

text_en:
Foreword
The operating instructions are to be distributed to those persons responsible for
operating and monitoring the device.
The operating instructions contain the information necessary for installation, operation and maintenance.
Those tasks not requiring special knowledge or skills were not included in the instructions.
Repair instructions above and beyond the regular maintenance tasks to be performed are not provided in the instructions.
Important notes
•
Receiving Inspection
Immediately upon receipt, perform a visual inspection of the control unit as defined by the delivery contract.
•
Storage
If the control unit will not immediately be installed in its final destination, store
the unit in a protected location to prevent damage due to weather and foreign
material.
•
Installation
All installation specifications delivered along with the control unit must be followed during installation.
•
Model types
Should the documentation provided with the control unit describe other versions of the unit, only that information which pertains to the version of the control unit that was delivered to the recipient shall apply. All features and specifications are subject to technical modification without notice prior to shipment.
•
Duty of instruction
The unit may only be operated and maintained by trained and qualified personnel. Prior to initial operation, all personnel that will be operating the unit
must familiarize themselves with the documentation provided.
Further documentation
Other documents are available for reference:

breadcrumb: MEAG Automatic Volume Controller (FBAL) Operating Instructions > 1.1 Intended use > Hal. 5
text_en:
Safety
Note:
The operating instructions must be kept near the control unit.
1.1
Intended use
The control unit is intended to control only the device shown on the title page of
this document.
It is not intended for any other use.
1.2
Duty of instruction
The operator is responsible for the training and safety of the operating personnel.
For this reason, it is very important that these operating instructions actually be distributed to these persons.
Operating personnel responsible for the installation, operation or maintenance of
the control unit must have read and understood these operating instructions.
1.3
Accident prevention
The control unit complies with the international safety standard.
For your own safety, please observe all accident prevention and safety regulations
that are contained in these operating instructions and that apply locally.
Note:
Warning and instruction plates must be kept clean and must not be removed or
covered.
Immediately replace any illegible warning and instruction plates.
1.4
Operation
The control unit may only be operated by instructed and trained personnel. Personnel must be familiar with all display and operational elements.
1.5
Electrical installation
Have authorized personnel perform the installation procedures.
•
Observe regulations issued by local safety authorities.
•
Secure the supply lines according to local regulations.
•
Check the operating voltage and frequency with respect to the information provided on the identification plate and in the control cabinet.
•
Connect the control unit power supply according to the connection diagram.
•
When setting up or repairing the control unit, make sure that the power supply
is interrupted by disconnecting all poles and that it cannot be restarted.
Check the electrical installation on a regular basis.
•
Repair or replace defective installations or devices immediately.

text_en: Commissioning Basic parameters are configured ex works. Note: To change the parameters, the control unit must be in step 0 (Calibrating) or step 1 (Standby). (For current step, see WT.) Stop the flow balancer to do this. The control process can also be forced into step 0. Set the calibration switch to CAL and turn the input voltage on and off. 4.1 Basic settings 1. Parameter SYS.TYP = FBAL, continue with number 4. 2. Set SYS.TYP parameter to FBAL (can only be adjusted when calibration switch is set to CAL). The unit is restarted automatically. 3. Select SYS.TYP parameter. Press "F" key (S4). The input assistant is activated. Select each parameter directly by pressing the arrow key. The assistant is automatically exited after the last parameter. 4. If the flow balancer's setpoints are being configured remotely, set the SYS.REM parameter (analog, serial, or Profibus). 4.2 Flow balancer alignment 1. Turn on the control unit. Wait at least 10 minutes before beginning the calibration process. 2. Set the calibration switch S2 on the main circuit board to CAL. 3. Zeroing = impact plate without weight. 4. Zero: with the ADC.ZERO parameter by pressing the "F" key. A rotating clock symbol is displayed. Do not interfere with the flow balancer while it is being zeroed. 5. Enter the calibration weight under the ADC.CALW parameter. MZAH-10/ -12/ -15 = 3000 kg, MZAH-25 = 2 x 3000 kg. 6. Calibration weights should be mounted symmetrically onto the places provided on the impact plate. 7. Calibrate using the ADC.CALW parameter by pressing the "F" key. A rotating clock symbol is displayed. Do not interfere with the flow balancer while it is being calibrated. 8. Using the ADC.WT parameter, check the weight display for the calibration weight. 9. Remove the calibration weights. 10. The weight displayed

breadcrumb: MEAG Automatic Volume Controller (FBAL) Operating Instructions > 5.1 Operating modes > Hal. 20
text_en: Functional description 5.1 Operating modes Flowmeter (FLOMET) Flow rate measurement and flow volume in an external product flow In this operating mode, the flow rate is measured on the basis of the amount of product deflected at the impact plate. After start (Enable), the metering slide gate remains open. Flow controller (FLOCON) Metering from the full (silo) In this operating mode, product is metered from the full silo in accordance with the preselectable feed rate. The metering slide gate is moved into the corresponding position. 5.2 Set of steps Once the flow balancer has been turned on, steps 3 through 6 are executed in cycles Step Meaning Description Standby The control waits for a feeder to be enabled. Feeder stop The metering slide gate closes in its home position (for approx. 20 s the "Slide gate quickly closed" function is activated). Zeroing Zero the measuring section after CLOSING. Metering slide gate is closed. Metering The throughput is controlled depending on the nominal / actual deviation. Transient response Period of waiting before measurement. Measuring time During the measuring time, the measurement points for calculating the rate are saved. The measuring time and number of measurement points are automatically selected depending on the nominal rate and the current control range. Calculations Calculation of actual flow rate. The control signal for the 4 pilot valves is calculated and output. Leak test Testing pressure drop during measuring time. Once the measuring time has passed, the result gained from the test appears on the display. Valve test Function test for valve group (Activation of metering slide gate). This test consists of a visual check of measuring distances (Home and current metering slide gate position). Calibrating The calibration switch S2 is on "CAL". Only during this step is it possible to adjust the weight or make

text_en: 5.6.5 SERV Menu Code Lock Parameter group SERV (service information) Attr. Range ID Identification text is displayed. Text is transmitted by a host. It is possible to display max. 28 characters (second part with the "F" key). e.g., B1 SCALE V_PROG Programme version, complete programme, application and basis system. e.g., V10A V_APPL Version and name of the application (according to SYS.TYP). e.g., V10A V_BASE Version of the basic system (application-independent software). e.g., V10A V_BOOT Bootloader version e.g., V10A DATE L Date 01.01.00… 31.12.99 TIME L Time 00.00.00… 23.59.59 ERR List of alarms The last alarm will be displayed as ERR.0 A006 . Older alarms can be displayed by pressing the "F" and "-" keys. The second-to-last alarm will be displayed as ERR.-1, etc. Go back to the previous alarm by pressing the "F" and "+" keys. By pressing only the "F" key, it is possible to switch between the entire alarm message, date and time. EVT List of events The last event will be displayed as EVT.0 E001 . For operation, see parameter ERR. ALLEVT List of alarms and events Alarms and events are both shown. For operation, see parameter ERR. CPU Computer load Displayed on the left: Current computer load in %. Displayed on the right: Max. time in ms for a programme cycle. If necessary, max. value can be reset by pressing the "F" key. Voltage is too low (<18 V)
−
Measure the voltage on X1.
−

text_en:
A006
DATALOST
Loss of data
Loss of data in the battery-buffered RAM.
The parameters and diverse data are initialised to their default values.
May occur once after a software download.
−
Check the fit of the battery base.
−
Acknowledge the alarm if new software
was loaded.
−
To acknowledge the alarm:
Disconnect the control unit from the
mains.
Wait 15 min.
Turn on the control unit.
If the alarm is repeated, replace the
battery.

set it to 0.
−
Check the installation position of the
load cells.

doc_title: MEAG Automatic Volume Controller (FBAL) Operating Instructions
breadcrumb: MEAG Automatic Volume Controller (FBAL) Operating Instructions > 6.5 Operational status messages > Hal. 45
text_en:
6.5
Operational status messages
Operational status messages give an overview of the operational status of the device.
The messages are displayed alternately with the normal display and only as long
as the status lasts.
Alarms are of higher priority and overwrite operational status messages.
Message
Meaning
LOCAL STOP
Device has been stopped manually.
STOP
Device has been stopped because 0V is displayed on the 24V input "Enable/Start".
c STOP
Device has been stopped because no release is connected via Profibus or
RS-485 (HOST).
v STOP
Device has been stopped because the setpoint is too low.
∑ STOP
Device has been stopped because the required total or a required number
has been reached.
WAIT PRODUCT
Device has been started but no product is present (e.g., probe is uncovered).
REFILL
Fill function is active (abnormal filling).
DISCHARGE
Empty function (or residual discharge function) is active (abnormal discharge).
CAL MODE
CAL mode is active (switch is in the CAL position).
SERVICE
Service mode is active (outputs may be set).
LOCAL
Device is being operated locally (only if REMOTE input is active and 0 V is
on).
MANUAL
Device is being operated manually (control operations not occurring automatically).
EMERGENCY
Device is running in emergency mode.
TEACHING
Device is running in teaching mode.
HIGH SETP
Setpoint is too high. The setpoint is set at the maximum value.
SIM ON
Simulator mode is on and active.
SIM FREEZE
Simulator mode is on but passive.
TEST
Device is running in test mode.
LOW SETP
Setpoint is too low. Setpoint is set at the minimum or at 0.
WARM UP
Wait until the AD converter is stable.

doc_title: MEAG Automatic Volume Controller (FBAL) Operating Instructions
breadcrumb: MEAG Automatic Volume Controller (FBAL) Operating Instructions > 6.6 Updates > Hal. 46
text_en:
6.6
Updates
Updates serve to help during operation of the device. They appear only once when
a key is pressed.
Message
Meaning
Applications
OK
Input has been recognized and accepted.
E.g., when a recipe is loaded.
LOCK
The edit parameter function is locked.
E.g., the edit parameter function is
locked with SYS.LOCK.
PROTECT
Recipes are protected from being
overwritten. The save recipe function
is locked.
E.g., recipe overwrite protection
REC.PROT = ON
DATA INIT
Perform the initialization process.
Caution: Parameters are being set to
default values.
With SYS.INIT
SET ZERO
Perform zeroing.
E.g., during the zeroing process
(ADC.ZERO)
SET CAL
Perform calibration.
E.g., during calibration (ADC.CALW)
SET TARE
Perform tare procedure.
E.g., when taring DMS-T
WT INIT
Reinitialize weight values.
Caution: Data may be lost.
E.g., when ADC.DIV is adjusted.
WAIT
Please wait until the WAIT message
has disappeared.
CLEAR
Data are being erased.
E.g., event reports.
ESC
Editing cancelled.
"LT" key was pressed during the editing
process.
OCCUPIED
Interface is busy.
E.g., when SIO is connected to the host
interface and must be reconnected to
an external device.
NO EDIT
Edit function is not possible.
E.g., display parameters (may never be
edited).
NO CAL
Editing may only take place in CAL
mode.
E.g., display parameters (may not be
edited).
NO LOCAL
Editing may only take place in LOCAL
mode.
E.g., display parameters (may not be
edited).
NO STOP
Editing may only take place when the
device has been stopped.
E.g., display parameters (may not be
edited).
NO SETVAL
No setpoint is present.
E.g., it is possible to start the device
without a setpoint.
ASSIST ON
The input assistant has been turned
on.
ASSIST OFF
The input assistant has been turned
off.
OUT OF
RANGE
The value that was entered lies outside of the possible setting range.
